exposure: intracervical Foley catheter for induction of labour
intracervical Dinoprostone gel for induction of labour
cohort: 220 pregnant women with singleton, cephalic, term pregnancies (37-41 weeks) and a Bishop score < 6.
finding: Mechanical induction with a Foley catheter significantly reduced the risk of uterine hyperstimulation compared to Dinoprostone gel, while pharmacological induction resulted in a significantly shorter induction-to-delivery interval.
mod_finding: The rate of Cesarean section was lower in the mechanical induction group (18.2%) compared to the pharmacological induction group (23.6%), though this difference was not statistically significant.
